title: Birds can get jet lag on long, fast flights and then fly off course | New Scientist
description: On fast flights across the Atlantic, the body clocks of Manx shearwaters get out of sync with local time, leading them to veer away from the most direct flight path
author: Michael Le Page

title: Inhaling CO2 may rescue nerves’ ability to regrow | New Scientist
description: Breathing out after birth switches off the ability of tissues to regenerate, a study in mice suggests. But the pathway seems to be reversible
author: Jo Marchant

title: Key oddity of quantum physics may run even deeper than anticipated | New Scientist
description: Quantum mechanics stands out by being probabilistic and a new analysis suggests that this property can be traced unexpectedly deep into the theory’s mathematical foundations
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Why the world's first spinal cord transplant is so controversial | New Scientist
description: A spinal cord transplant happened in people for the first time during a surgery in Russia, but the evidence underpinning it is lacking
author: New Scientist

title: There may be a new dwarf planet just beyond Pluto | New Scientist
description: Astronomers spotted what appears to be a dwarf planet in the outer solar system using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory – if confirmed, it joins a small and exclusive club
author: Leah Crane

title: Access to stone as well as water governed where early humans lived | New Scientist
description: The sands of the Arabian peninsula were once dotted with lakes that teemed with life, but early humans avoided them unless they came with easy access to stone for tool-making
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre
